title: Lacunarity and generalized lacunarity for binary time series
text: simulate Bernoulli series 80%80\% ones compute lacunarity. Ds decreases towards 11 scale grows, signature essentially homogeneous (gap-poor) pattern. decay clearest log–log plot:
code: x <- rbinom(2000, size = 1, prob = 0.8) rx <- lac(x) rx #> $y #> [1] 0.01311362 #>  #> $Ds #> [1] 1.130717 1.067124 1.036955 1.020647 1.011371 #>  #> $s #>      [,1] #> [1,]    2 #> [2,]    4 #> [3,]    8 #> [4,]   16 #> [5,]   32 plot(rx$s, rx$Ds, log = "xy", type = "b", pch = 19,      xlab = "scale s", ylab = expression(Lambda(s)),      main = "Lacunarity curve of a random binary series") abline(h = 1, lty = 2, col = "grey50")

title: Lacunarity and generalized lacunarity for binary time series
text: point lacunarity density alone determine texture. , z strongly clustered sequence (blocks ones zeros) w random shuffle z: exactly number ones, hence density, different spatial organisation. clustered series substantially larger lacunarity every scale:  Although z w indistinguishable mean, Λ(s)\Lambda(s) cleanly separates blocky texture random one — exactly information density second-order summaries miss.
code: block <- c(rep(c(rep(1, 8),  rep(0, 8)),  60),            rep(c(rep(1, 16), rep(0, 16)), 60)) z <- block w <- sample(block)               # same ones, gaps reshuffled  mean(z) == mean(w)               # identical density #> [1] TRUE  lz <- lac(z) lw <- lac(w) c(clustered = lz$y, shuffled = lw$y) #>  clustered   shuffled  #> 0.19072431 0.07468284 ylim <- range(lz$Ds, lw$Ds) plot(lz$s, lz$Ds, log = "xy", type = "b", pch = 19, ylim = ylim,      xlab = "scale s", ylab = expression(Lambda(s)),      main = "Same density, different lacunarity") lines(lw$s, lw$Ds, type = "b", pch = 1, lty = 2) legend("topright", c("clustered", "shuffled"),        pch = c(19, 1), lty = c(1, 2), bty = "n")

title: Lacunarity and generalized lacunarity for binary time series
text: Finally compare spectra γ(q)\gamma(q) clustered random series genlac().  clustered series produces spectrum varies markedly qq — multilacunar texture terminology Vernon-Carter et al. (2009), small large gaps scale differently. shuffled series gives nearly flat spectrum, monofractal signature structureless, single-scale gap distribution.
code: gz <- genlac(z) gw <- genlac(w)  plot(gz$q, gz$yq, type = "b", pch = 19,      xlab = "moment order q", ylab = expression(gamma(q)),      main = "Generalized lacunarity spectrum",      ylim = range(gz$yq, gw$yq)) lines(gw$q, gw$yq, type = "b", pch = 1, lty = 2) legend("topleft", c("clustered", "shuffled"),        pch = c(19, 1), lty = c(1, 2), bty = "n")
